truth_boundary: Engineering sizing screen for CAD completeness. Not certification, FEA, dynamic contact simulation, or physical validation.

joint_and_linkage_assumptions.selected_rod_end_family_SRC: Aurora AM-M10T metric male PTFE-lined rod end
joint_and_linkage_assumptions.selected_lock_nut_family_SRC: DIN 985 / ISO 10511 prevailing torque lock nut

combined_climb_assumptions.local_drive_suspension_loop: Sub-millisecond motor/suspension command loop; preview sensors feed a predictive stair phase map and are not waited on at the stair edge.
combined_climb_assumptions.control_mode: Sensor-previewed predictive corner prepositioning plus sub-millisecond local wheel torque and suspension control; not wheel-only climbing.

smooth_climb_assumptions.preview_treads_reason: ifm O1D100 preview sensor (data/te_v059_sourced_part_register.json, id stair_preview_distance_sensor) has a 0.2-10 m measuring range, far beyond the 0.2794 m stair going; 2 treads of lookahead (0.559 m) stays well inside that range while giving a jerk-limited blend enough time budget instead of reacting at the stair edge.
smooth_climb_assumptions.chassis_ramp_error_budget_reason: How far the chassis corner may deviate from the ideal ramp line before the ride stops being 'ramp-like'. 25 mm is about 12% of the 203.2 mm stair rise -- i.e. the smoothed path removes ~88% of the raw step. Originally chosen as an engineering target with no standard behind it; since checked against ISO 2631-1 and found to be well-calibrated rather than arbitrary -- see chassis_ramp_error_budget_iso_2631_check below and data/te_v059_ride_quality_trade_study.json.

chassis_ramp_error_budget_iso_2631_check.standard_SRC: ISO 2631-1:1997, Mechanical vibration and shock -- Evaluation of human exposure to whole-body vibration, Part 1: General requirements. Comfort reaction bands (weighted RMS m/s^2): <=0.315 not uncomfortable; 0.315-0.63 a little uncomfortable; 0.5-1.0 fairly uncomfortable; 0.8-1.6 uncomfortable; 1.25-2.5 very uncomfortable; >2.0 extremely uncomfortable.
chassis_ramp_error_budget_iso_2631_check.source_confidence: The comfort bands above are consistently reported across multiple secondary sources summarising the standard, but the primary ISO document was NOT obtained (paywalled; the public preview PDF is not machine-readable). The Wk frequency-weighting curve values could not be verified from a primary source at all and are therefore NOT used below. Purchase the primary standard before any release claim rests on this.
chassis_ramp_error_budget_iso_2631_check.method_CALC: The chassis ramp error repeats once per stair tread, so at the mandated 0.2 m/s forward speed over a 279.4 mm going it is periodic at a stair-passing frequency of 0.7158 Hz. For a single tone, acceleration follows exactly from displacement: a_peak = A*(2*pi*f)^2, a_rms = a_peak/sqrt(2). max|ramp error| is treated as the amplitude A.
chassis_ramp_error_budget_iso_2631_check.unweighted_note: Both figures are UNWEIGHTED. ISO 2631-1's Wk curve attenuates below about 4 Hz, so the correctly weighted values are lower than these -- each absolute number is therefore conservative (pessimistic about comfort). Critically, because the budget and the achieved error sit at the same frequency, their 3.44x ratio is independent of whatever the correct Wk factor turns out to be.
chassis_ramp_error_budget_iso_2631_check.finding: The 25 mm budget converts to 0.358 m/s^2 unweighted, essentially sitting on the ISO 2631-1 'not uncomfortable' ceiling of 0.315 m/s^2 -- and below it once Wk attenuation at 0.72 Hz is applied. It is a well-calibrated target, not a lax or arbitrary one. The achieved 86.1 mm converts to 1.232 m/s^2, landing in the 'uncomfortable' band, for a child occupant. Relaxing the budget to make ride_quality pass is therefore NOT defensible against the real standard; this route to closure is closed.
chassis_ramp_error_budget_iso_2631_check.OPEN: A rigorous ISO 2631-1 evaluation requires frequency-weighted RMS over the real acceleration time history, which needs a dynamic model with tire and passive spring/damper compliance. The current kinematic screen cannot supply it: its raw chassis acceleration channel is dominated by a differentiation artifact of the non-smooth wheel-over-nosing geometry (it reports ~108 g, bit-identical to the uncorrected bare-stair value). Closes with the PyBullet rigid-body contact simulation already on the task list.
